title: Is Your Attitude to AI Holding You Back?
author: Salles, Dominic
summary: Dominic Salles argues that most resistance to AI is social prejudice rather than rational evaluation, and that AI is already producing high-quality results most people underestimate. He lists his own weekly teaching uses across creative writing, lesson planning, research, revision materials, and feedback tasks—all at beginner level, no coding required. He closes with a reveal: the viral 'bad AI' Monet that received 6 million views and 1,300 disgusted reactions was an actual Renoir-era Monet painting.
points: Resistance to AI typically stems from social prejudice absorbed from deliberately selected failure examples on social media rather than from direct evaluation of AI output.
Practical daily AI uses for teachers include: creative writing, teaching scripts, deep research, lesson planning, feedback evaluation, dictation, and revision card creation—all beginner-level.
Tools like NotebookLM enable source-restricted research and lesson planning; Claude and Gemini are best for writing, editing, and adapting content to a specific tone.
The gap between what AI can produce and what people believe it produces is widened by negative social media examples chosen specifically to represent AI at its worst.
The Monet test: a viral image with 6 million views and 1,300 complaints calling it AI slop was a genuine Monet painting—illustrating how ingrained prejudice overrides direct perception.
quotes: Writing resources only using sources I trust - NotebookLM Creating lesson plans or schemes of work based on Rosenshine and sources I trust - NotebookLM Deciding which written response is better and why, for feedback - Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT Dictating all my ideas as I ramble - Whisperflow and Apple Notes Turning my ramblings into something useful.
There are dozens of everyday uses as a writer and YouTuber, and many more for understanding how to do something, find something, fix something, etc.
The point is that I think this because AI right now, never mind what staggering advance it makes in the future, is already bloody brilliant.
I truly believe AI is going to destroy jobs and disrupt economies - whether I am right or not is not the point.
How I Use AI as a Teacher and School Improvement Partner These are my favourite uses of AI at the minute.
